correctness.rationale: Strict negativity of each invasion payoff at e_j is equivalent almost surely to pure ESS, and given its diagonal D_j the N-1 outside comparisons are independent with acceptance probability Phi(D_j/sqrt(v_mu)). Independent row maxima give the zero-ratio endpoint. For m=N-1>=2 the symmetrized integrand z on |Z| involves p^m+(1-p)^m, strictly increasing for p=Phi(t|Z|)>1/2 as t=v_mu^(-1/2) increases; this independently proves the monotonicity direction. The expectation is even in t with bounded second derivative near zero, giving O_N(mu^-2) one-site error. For each pair the independent Gaussian antisymmetric contrast has density 1/sqrt(pi) at zero, interval width (D_i+D_j-2U)_+/(1+2mu), and the N-2 outside tests for each resident multiply to leading term 4^(-(N-2)). The width numerator is the positive part of N(0,4), of mean sqrt(2/pi). Bounded Gaussian CDF derivatives, finite moments and the Lipschitz estimate for the outside factors give the claimed integrable O_N(mu^-2) pair error. At least two independent contrast intervals are required for a triple, so its error bound suffices: summing one-site probabilities and distinct pair overlaps gives probabilities 1-q_N+C_N/mu, q_N-2C_N/mu and C_N/mu at the stated precision. The N=2 orthant law reduces to arctan(1/sqrt(v_mu))/pi, independently confirming its leading constant (python /workspace/branches/independent-algebra.py, item 4). All probability comparisons are fixed-N and count pure ESSs only; the script spot check is not an all-N proof.

evidence: Nassor et al. enumerate all supports in their numerical methodology and report outcomes with N=10, M=10000. Figs. 15–16 concern the overall ESS multiplicity and sizes as the ratio varies, not an exact pure count or first rare-multiplicity coefficient. The sign tournament at the antisymmetric limit forbids two pure winners but gives no rate.

The package compares Madec–Gjini's model and antisymmetric limit and Chawanya–Tokita's antisymmetric dynamics. The fresh lawful full-text attempts did not yield usable text for these two works; those works are not categorically excluded.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The presence of all supports in simulations does not imply an analytic probability for the strict pure-support statistic. A limiting antisymmetry theorem alone cannot specify a first nonzero correction.

evidence: The iid row-maximum theorem gives the asserted count at mu=0 and the independent sign tournament accounts for q_N only. In the model at positive mu simultaneous success of a pair uses both directions of the same Gaussian contrast, and the narrow interval has a width depending jointly on the diagonals and the symmetric part.
The first coefficient requires the mean positive width times the outside comparison probability. Neither an exact iid result nor the same structured ensemble's simulation/limit provides it.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The earlier endpoint result is fully credited. The stated positive-ratio trichotomy is not a corollary of taking the antisymmetric limit, which discards the symmetric terms that determine that coefficient.

evidence: Nassor et al. use resident-first indices, so reindexing Eq. (22) reproduces the assigned ensemble exactly. Hart–Rinott–Weiss state the iid continuous pure-ESS count Binomial(n,1/n). At mu=0 the assigned matrix is an iid Gaussian payoff matrix (transposed raw array) with a resident-specific column constant subtracted; this leaves each resident's strict payoff comparisons unchanged. Thus Hart's result covers the binomial endpoint, not merely a similar numerical law.
Hart's two-point ESSs are individual mixed strategies with support size two, not simultaneous distinct pure ESSs.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Column normalization gives exact equivalence at zero ratio, but not for mu>0 when opposite comparisons remain correlated even before normalization. The distinction is the positive-ratio law and first nonzero correction, not the iid endpoint.

originality.rationale: The zero-ratio binomial law and the limiting tournament probability are existing coverage. The distinct contribution is fixed-N positive-ratio Gaussian expectation together with the explicit inverse-ratio rare-pair coefficient and resulting trichotomy. The exact same-ensemble primary model and all-support simulations do not give that finite-ratio analytic law. Bounded search does not establish historical priority.
residual_risks: General Gaussian orthant or near-tournament literature might contain an equivalent fixed-size correction. The targeted primary search supplied the known iid source and model antecedent, not a comprehensive priority result.
Full texts for Madec–Gjini and Chawanya–Tokita are not independently resolved. The exact iid endpoint and universal-winner limit must not be presented as new.
